preamble: Diphthongization of the nasal vowel [õ] into a back nasal diphthong [õw̃] or [ɔw̃] (mapped to the ou cell). Polish ą, historically a nasal monophthong from Proto-Slavic *ǫ, is now pronounced [ɔw̃] before non-palatal fricatives and word-finally (są 'they are'). In Brazilian and European Portuguese the word-final nasal vowel of bom 'good' and som 'sound' is commonly realized [õw̃], although whether it is a true diphthong is disputed.

examples.note: Before non-palatal fricatives (f, w, s, z, sz, ż, rz, ch) and word-finally ą is an oral vowel plus a nasalized glide [w̃]; before stops it splits into vowel + nasal consonant instead.
Word-final -om (bom, som 'sound') is listed as [õw̃] ~ [õ]; the diphthongal analysis is controversial.

sources: Wikipedia contributors. Portuguese phonology, section Nasal diphthongs. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_phonology
